introduction-taming-the-tool-sprawl.core: Developers juggle dozens of tools (CI, cloud consoles, dashboards, wikis, ticketing) to do simple tasks. An Internal Developer Platform with a portal like Backstage gives one place to find, create and operate services.

first_principles.problem: To ship a feature, a developer visits 12 different tools and asks 4 people for links.
truths: Context switching between tools costs time.
derivation: Add **plugins and self-service actions**; **TechDocs** for docs.

analogy.title: A chaotic kitchen vs. an organised one
analogy.story: Running between rooms for each ingredient versus a well-organised station with everything at hand.
analogy.breaks: A portal over a weak platform is just a pretty facade, so the engine matters most.

example.title: One task, before and after a portal
flow: Before: GitHub, Grafana, PagerDuty, Confluence, Slack
After: Backstage entity page shows owner, docs, dashboards, on-call, CI

check.q: What problem does an internal developer portal primarily address?
check.a: Tool sprawl and scattered information that force developers to context-switch across many systems.

the-portal-vs-the-platform.core: The platform is the engine (APIs, infrastructure automation, golden paths, policies). The portal is the dashboard (UI like Backstage). A portal without a platform only links out; a platform without a portal can still be used through CLIs and APIs.

first_principles.problem: Teams install Backstage and call it a platform, but every action still needs a ticket behind the scenes.
truths: Many interfaces can front one platform.
derivation: Keep the **portal thin** over solid engines.

analogy.title: A car's dashboard vs. its engine
analogy.story: A beautiful dashboard on a car with no engine doesn't drive anywhere.
analogy.breaks: Portals do add real value through discoverability and catalogue information, even with modest automation.

example.title: A 'create database' feature
flow: Platform: Crossplane composition provisions RDS + secrets
example.outcome: clarity about what makes a platform real.

check.q: Why isn't installing Backstage the same as having a platform?
check.a: Backstage is a portal (UI); without automated platform capabilities underneath, it just links to manual processes.

backstage-pillar-1-the-software-catalog.core: The Backstage software catalogue registers every component, API, resource, system and owner through catalog-info.yaml files kept in each repo, answering 'who owns this, where are its docs, what does it depend on?'.

first_principles.problem: In a company with hundreds of microservices, nobody can quickly find who owns payments-api or what calls it.
truths: Metadata near the code stays current.

analogy.title: A city directory
analogy.story: Every building listed with its owner, purpose, address and connections.
analogy.breaks: The catalogue rots if ownership changes aren't reflected, so automate validation.

example.title: A catalogue descriptor

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Owner, on-call, repo and dependencies in one place.

code.text:
apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: payments-api
  annotations: { pagerduty.com/service-id: P123, github.com/project-slug: acme/payments-api }
spec:
  type: service
  lifecycle: production
  owner: team-payments
  system: checkout
  dependsOn: [resource:payments-db]

example.outcome: every piece of software findable and owned.

check.q: Where does Backstage catalogue metadata usually live?
check.a: In a catalog-info.yaml file in each component's repository.

backstage-pillar-2-scaffolding-and-templ.core: Software templates (the scaffolder) create new projects from golden-path templates in minutes: repo, CI/CD, Dockerfile, catalogue registration, docs and observability, all pre-wired. Best practice becomes the default starting point.

first_principles.problem: Starting a new service takes days of copy-pasting from an old repo, plus tickets for CI, monitoring and access.
truths: Starting from good defaults spreads standards.
Templates can encode the organisation's best practices.
derivation: Run **actions**: create repo, push, register in catalogue, open PR.

analogy.title: A pre-furnished apartment
analogy.story: Move in with furniture, utilities and Wi-Fi ready, instead of furnishing an empty room.
analogy.breaks: Templates only set the starting point, so existing services drift unless updated.

example.title: Creating a new Go service
flow: Repo created with CI, Helm chart, catalog-info, TechDocs
First deploy to staging in 15 minutes
example.outcome: new services that start on the golden path.

check.q: What does the Backstage scaffolder do?
check.a: It creates new projects from templates, automating repo creation, CI/CD setup and catalogue registration.

backstage-pillar-3-plugins-and-self-serv.core: Plugins bring operational data and actions into the portal (Kubernetes status, CI runs, cost, PagerDuty, ArgoCD), and self-service actions let developers restart pods, request databases or rotate secrets without tickets, within guardrails.

first_principles.problem: Every operational task ('restart my pod', 'give me a DB') needs a ticket to the platform team and waits for days.
truths: Context in one place speeds debugging.
derivation: Add **plugins** for the key tools (K8s, CI, observability, cost).
Build **self-service actions** backed by platform APIs.

analogy.title: Self-checkout with a supervisor nearby
analogy.story: Customers serve themselves quickly, while guardrails prevent misuse.
analogy.breaks: Plugin sprawl can make the portal slow and confusing, so curate it.

example.title: From ticket to self-service
flow: After: portal form → Crossplane claim → DB ready in 8 min

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: The platform team stops being a ticket queue.

check.q: What's the main benefit of self-service actions in a developer portal?
check.a: Developers perform common operational tasks instantly within guardrails, instead of waiting on tickets.

techdocs-documentation-as-code.core: TechDocs renders Markdown docs that live in each service's repo (MkDocs) inside Backstage, next to the catalogue entry. Docs are reviewed in PRs, versioned with the code and discoverable, which ends the stale-wiki graveyard.

first_principles.problem: The Confluence wiki is 60% outdated and 30% duplicated, so nobody trusts it.
truths: Docs near code get updated with code.
PR review applies to docs too.
derivation: **Search** across all docs in the portal.

analogy.title: Instructions printed on the product itself
analogy.story: Instead of a manual lost in a drawer, the instructions travel with the device.
analogy.breaks: Docs-as-code still needs writing discipline, because co-location helps but doesn't guarantee quality.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: The service page shows current docs from main.

code.text:
metadata:
  annotations:
    backstage.io/techdocs-ref: dir:.
# repo: mkdocs.yml + docs/index.md

check.q: Why does docs-as-code reduce documentation staleness?
check.a: Docs live with the code and are updated and reviewed in the same PRs as code changes.
